scope: Installed Codex CLI v0.155.1 command hooks for SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, and Stop; no product code or hook configuration was changed

startState.priorCandidateDisposition: Unmerged and unpushed; W06-a-codex-r1 remains BLOCKED

releaseIdentity.binding: The installed Windows binary SHA-256 exactly matches the official v0.155.1 release asset digest. The release tag dereferences to the inspected source commit. This is a release-source correspondence, not a local rebuild or proof of every runtime deployment setting.

priorLinuxObservation.npmProvenanceStatement: The fetched npm attestation payload names refs/tags/rust-v0.155.1 and source commit be2951ea34f0d295ed0becf97079f92fa5f6950e for @openai/codex@0.155.1-linux-x64. Its signature was not independently verified in this task, and this package is supporting version context rather than the primary source pin.

commandHookTrace.finding: SessionStart serializes session_id, transcript_path, cwd, event name, model, permission_mode, and source; it has no turn_id. UserPromptSubmit and Stop serialize a turn_id alongside ordinary event fields. None of these schema types contains an attestation, host process identity, signature, or independent provenance handle.

The event handlers pass serialized input_json into the dispatcher. Synchronous local handlers invoke execute_handler with metadata None; its Command arm passes command, configured env, input_json, and cwd into run_command. Asynchronous command handlers instead use schedule_async_hook, which calls run_command with those same inputs; its turn_id is used by result parsing after the child run. Executor-scoped metadata and the McpTool arm are separate paths.

run_command creates a configured shell child with piped stdin/stdout/stderr, spawns it, and writes input_json bytes to child stdin. build_command supplies the configured command line and replays the session environment snapshot plus hook-configured env. The inspected command-child path passes no separate authenticated process-and-turn channel.

documentedVersusAuthenticated.documented: Command hook event JSON arrives on stdin; turn_id is an exposed field for some events.
documentedVersusAuthenticated.authenticated: Neither the documentation nor the inspected v0.155.1 command hook source defines a verifier or independent attestation for a child hook to bind the host executable identity and turn to that JSON. A child can read the fields, but the fields alone do not prove origin to a separately invoked verifier.
notAttestation: stdin event JSON or its turn_id and a hash of that value
argv or environment values copied into the child
PID, parent or ancestor relationship, process basename codex, or a matching path string
successful execution under the official CLI during a benign observation

adjacentPathBoundary.finding: McpTool hooks are dispatched on a different arm, and CoreHookMcpExecutor adds a threadId to MCP request metadata. That metadata is not supplied to the command child; threadId is not the required process-and-turn attestation. This task did not establish an alternative MCP tool hook protocol satisfying the W06-a-codex command hook contract.

determination.productDisposition: W06-a-codex remains BLOCKED; do not start implementation or promote the existing candidate
determination.reason: The pinned v0.155.1 command hook receives ordinary serialized JSON and configured process inputs, with no separate verifiable host-origin process-and-turn channel exposed by the inspected dispatch and child execution path.
determination.falsifier: A pinned v0.155.1 source location or reproducible installed-release observation showing a separate authenticated host process plus turn claim delivered to and verifiable by the command hook child would overturn this scoped conclusion. A turn_id field, matching PID, or codex executable name alone would not.
